chapter: To the US and the Caribbean with Carmen and Rolando
title: Chano Pozo and Cacha versus Carmen and Rolando
summary: The two dance acts had different styles, and Chano Pozo composed his own music and was a showman.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Speaking of the show, tell me your impressions of Chano Pozo and Cacha’s show? That is, what distinguished that couple’s show from the show of Carmen and Rolando of which you were a part.
Well, even though they were dancers, the trio of Carmen and Rolando and I, after the trio Chano with Cacha and Pepe were two different styles.

In the dance moves. Different - completely different. For there to be two couples in the same show, you normally do not see stuff like that. Because for example, people will say, "Well, two couples of dancers in the same show, what will be the difference? But there was indeed a difference because each one, each couple had their style, movement and music. And that was what made the success of the two couples was that they did not imitate each other.
The music for their show was mostly what kind?

Well, composed by Chano Pozo. And the music of Carmen and Rolando was another musical arranger, so even the music was different. Because Chano Pozo was a very good composer, a very good conga player, a very good composer and was a showman, he was a showman.
